untitled_hint: Not saved yet: Save asks for a file name.
theme_title: Theme: as the system, light or dark
start_lead: Start from a published formulation, or open a script you saved.
loaded: Loaded. Check the Materials tab, then Run.
chip_reactant: A reactant of the phase list: it dissolves into the paste. × leaves it out.
chip_product: A phase the paste may form. × leaves it out.
chip_removed: Left out of the list. ↺ takes it back.
chip_added: Added to the list. × removes it.
chip_custom: A phase of the system. × removes it.
chip_solid_solution: A solid solution: its end-members mix in one phase.
species_lead: Search by name, formula or cement notation; the elements keep the species made of them only.
species_builtin_only: The species of an imported database are listed once it is read by a calculation.
species_loading: The species appear once the compute process is ready.
elements_hint: Keep the species made of the selected elements only.
outside_range: outside its data at this temperature
activity_model: Activity model of the pore solution
diagnosis_pending: The diagnosis runs once the compute process is ready.
diagnosis_after_problems: The diagnosis waits until the problems listed in the Calculation tab are fixed.
diagnosis_clean: Nothing to report on the species and the data.
materials_lead: The binder: published materials, or your own from an oxide analysis or a mineral composition.
fraction_sum: The binder fractions add up to {total}.
degree_hint: The degree of reaction is the fraction of a constituent that has reacted, from 0 to 1.
constituents_pending: The constituents appear once the catalog of ChemistryLab is read.
mix_lead: The water, the temperature and the amount of binder of the paste.
numbers_hint: Numbers separated by spaces or semicolons.
notation_hint: How the formula is read: C is CaO in cement notation, carbon otherwise.
copied_rows: Copied: paste it into a spreadsheet.
paste_placeholder: Paste rows from a spreadsheet or a CSV: a name, an amount, and optionally a unit.
title: Title of the study
mode_equilibrium_text: One equilibrium of the paste, at the degrees of reaction of the Materials tab.
mode_extents_text: Equilibria along a parameter: the age, a replacement, an added species, renewals of water, the temperature.
mode_kinetics_text: Rate equations integrated in time, the equilibrium solved at each step.
problem_fraction_not_positive: The fraction of {material} must be positive.
problem_fractions_sum: The binder fractions add up to {total}, not 1.
problem_out_of_range: {field} = {value} ({where}) is outside its range, from {min} to {max}.
problem_no_database_file: Choose the database file to import.
problem_two_gels: {gels} are models of one C-S-H gel: declare one of them.
problem_oxide_unit: An oxide analysis is entered in mass %; {material} has other units.
problem_oxide_total: The oxides of {material} add up to {total} %, more than 105 %.
problem_mineral_unit: A mineral composition is entered in mass %; {material} has other units.
problem_mineral_total: The minerals of {material} add up to {total} %, more than 100 %.
problem_tabulated_extent: The table of {constituent} in {material} needs as many degrees as ages, at least two, the ages increasing.
problem_parrott_killoh_phase: The law of Parrott and Killoh applies to C3S, C2S, C3A and C4AF, not to {constituent} ({material}).
problem_empty_path: The list of values of the calculation is empty.
problem_empty_solution: The attacking solution has no solute.
problem_solution_unit: The solutes of the attacking solution are given in mol/L or mmol/L.
problem_no_law_of_age: A path in time needs a degree of reaction that depends on the age (a law, not a constant).
problem_activity_not_positive: The activity of {species} must be positive.
problem_no_species: Name the species whose activity is held.
getting_ready_hint: The first launch prepares the environment of the calculations, then each session compiles its first calculation. You can fill in the forms meanwhile.
porosity_unknown: Unknown: a constituent left unreacted has no sourced density, so the volumes are unknown (see the Phases tab).
si_hint: Saturation index log(Q/K): 0 for a phase at equilibrium, negative for one that would dissolve, positive for one that would precipitate.
certificate_hint: What the solver proved about the answer.
copy_failed: The browser refused the copy: select the text instead.
failed_title: The compute process could not start.
catalog_failed: The catalog of ChemistryLab could not be read.
run_wait: Wait until the status is ready.
run_problems: Fix the problems listed in the Calculation tab first.
run_failed: The calculation failed: see the Output tab.
picker_open: Open a script written by the studio
picker_empty_save: Nothing here yet: type a name below.
hk_builtin: Downloaded from its publisher at the first use, then kept on this machine.
hk_imported: A ThermoFun, PHREEQC, Geochemist's Workbench, EQ3/6 or Reaktoro file on this machine.
hk_phase_list: The phases a published study lets a cement paste form, which you may change.
hk_custom: Every solid of the system chosen by hand, with the solid solutions.
hk_cemdata18: The model Cemdata18 is fitted with: KOH or NaOH as the background electrolyte.
hk_dilute: Every activity coefficient is 1: a dilute solution only.
hk_davies: Up to an ionic strength of about 0.5 mol/kg.
hk_truesdell_jones: Ion-size and extended terms per ion.
hk_llnl: The B-dot equation of the LLNL databases.
hk_sit: Specific ion interaction theory: one coefficient per pair of ions of opposite charge.
hk_pitzer: Concentrated solutions, with the parameters ChemistryLab ships.
hk_template: A composition published in a paper, shipped with ChemistryLab.
hk_oxides: Your oxide analysis (XRF), turned into clinker phases by Bogue's calculation, or kept as oxides.
hk_minerals: Your mineral composition (XRD-Rietveld), species of the database by mass.
hk_constant: The same degree at every age.
hk_logistic: A degree rising from its initial to its final value, half way at the half time.
hk_tabulated: Degrees measured at ages, interpolated between them.
hk_parrott_killoh: The hydration of a clinker phase by the law of Parrott and Killoh, with its published parameters.
hk_capped: Another law, held below a cap.
hk_hydration: The paste at each age, its degrees of reaction read at each.
hk_blend: The binder with a growing fraction of another material.
hk_carbonation: CO2 added to the paste, mole by mole.
hk_salt: A salt added to the paste; chlorides need a phase holding chlorine (Friedel's salt).
hk_titration: Any species or formula added to the paste.
hk_leaching: The pore solution replaced by pure water, step by step.
hk_attack: The pore solution replaced by an attacking solution, step by step.
hk_temperature_sweep: The same paste at several temperatures.
hk_water_sweep: The same binder with several amounts of water.
hk_fixed_ph: The pH is held, the budget of H+ left free.
hk_fixed_activity: The activity of a species is held: CO2@ for a partial pressure of CO2.
hk_saturated_curing: External water fills the pores the chemical shrinkage empties.
hk_adiabatic: No heat exchanged: the temperature follows the reaction.
h_gel: The solid solution standing for the C-S-H; one model only.
h_fraction: Mass fraction of the material in the binder; the fractions add up to 1.
f_extents: Degree of reaction of each constituent
f_material_extent: Degree of reaction of the whole material
h_density: Leave 0 when it is unknown: the volumes are then unknown.
h_powers_cap: The degree a sealed paste can reach with its water, after Powers.
h_binder_mass: The masses of the results are given for this mass of binder.
h_age: The age the laws of the degrees of reaction are read at.
kinetics_retcode: The integration ended with {retcode}: the run stops short of its horizon.
hk_kinetics: Each constituent with a rate law reacts as the law says; the others are at equilibrium, to their degree of reaction, from the start.
hk_parrott_killoh_avrami: Nucleation, then interaction, then diffusion, with the published parameters of the phase.
hk_waller: The reaction of a fly ash or a silica fume, with a characteristic time.
hk_first_order: A rate proportional to what is left of the constituent.
hk_custom_rate: A Julia expression giving the rate in mol/s, of T (K), P (Pa), t (s), n and n0 (mol, by species), lna (log activities) and key (this constituent).
hk_semi_adiabatic: The temperature of the paste follows the heat it releases, less what the cell loses to the room.
f_water_factor: Slowed by a lack of water (w/c)
h_expression: For instance 1.0e-7 * n[key], or k * (1 - n[key] / n0[key])^(2/3); return a zero of the type of the inputs (zero(T)), never 0.0.
problem_pk_rate_phase: The law of Parrott and Killoh has parameters for C3S, C2S, C3A and C4AF, not for {constituent}.
problem_rate_syntax: The rate law of {constituent} does not read as a Julia expression.
problem_no_rate: A kinetic run needs a rate law for at least one constituent.
problem_ages_beyond_horizon: The ages to report go beyond the {horizon} days of the run.
problem_kinetics_constraint: A kinetic run holds the temperature and the pressure only: choose no constraint.
h_heat_capacity: Of the vessel and the inert parts: the paste's own is added. An illustrative value: measure your cell's.
h_loss: The heat the cell loses per kelvin above the room. An illustrative value: measure your cell's.
h_tau: The time at which half of the material has reacted at the reference temperature; 0 keeps the published one.
h_water_factor: A clinker phase slows down once the water left cannot feed it (Parrott and Killoh's factor of w/c).
h_blaine: The fineness of the material; the published laws are written at their own reference fineness.
minerals_missing: The system lacks {minerals}, which this material holds: the calculation would stop.
plot_dtg_axis: % of the reference mass per K
tga_note: Each loss is spread over its window: the interval in which the literature reads it ({sources}), unless the Calculation tab sets another. A window says where a loss is attributed, not how a phase decomposes. The curve integrates to the water and carbon dioxide the solids hold.
h_loss_quadratic: The loss of the cell as a ΔT + b ΔT², b in W/K²; 0 for a loss linear in ΔT.
surface_lead: The sites of the published model of Guo et al. (2018) on the C-S-H, after the equilibrium: what the surface binds (calcium, alkalis, chloride) and its potential.
k_csh_surface: Sites of the C-S-H (Guo et al. 2018)
hk_csh_surface: The gel is frozen at its composition, the sites of the model are put on it, and the paste is solved again with them; portlandite must be present.
h_donnan: A layer of water on the diffuse layer that holds the ions the surface attracts; it needs a pore water thicker than itself and than the Debye length, as in a suspension.
h_thickness: In nanometers; 0 takes one Debye length of the pore solution.
surface_donnan: Excess in the Donnan layer ({water} g of water)
surface_note: The pore water is a film of {film} nm on the C-S-H, against a Debye length of {debye} nm. The published model counts its calcium on top of a gel whose Ca/Si already includes it, so that portlandite gives some up.
problem_surface_kinetics: The surface of the C-S-H follows an equilibrium or a path of equilibria, not a kinetic run.
tga_windows_lead: Each release of the solids, the water of a phase or its carbon dioxide, is spread over the interval in which the literature reads it. Any of them may be given an interval or a peak of your own; the releases of the paste are listed once it has been run.
tga_no_keys: Run the calculation once: the releases of its solids are listed here.
h_from: Where the release starts: none of it below.
h_to: Where the release ends: all of it out above.
h_midpoint: Where half of the release has happened.
h_width: The spread of the peak: 98 % of the release within 4.6 widths on either side of the midpoint.
problem_window_key: "{key}" names no release of the solids: a window is set for "<phase> (water)" or "<phase> (CO2)".
problem_window_order: The window of {key} ends at {to} °C, before it starts at {from} °C.
